ADAS.content:
This project focuses on developing a modular software platform for
Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS), aimed at enhancing vehicle safety
and automation. The primary objective is to create a robust system that
integrates multiple functionalities such as lane-keeping assistance, adaptive
cruise control, emergency braking, and pedestrian detection.

COMP_ADC_DRV.content:
Driver for the 12-bit ADC peripheral. Manages DMA-based sampling at
100Hz with double buffering, automatic averaging, and outlier
rejection. Channels:

- Channel 0: Temperature sensor (NTC thermistor)
- Channel 1: Water level sensor (capacitive)
COMP_ADC_DRV.title: ADC Driver

COMP_BREW_CTRL.content:
Module managing the brewing process state machine. States: IDLE,
HEATING, BREWING, COMPLETE, ERROR. Controls pump and valve timing
based on selected strength. Waits for temperature ready signal before
initiating brew cycle. Monitors safety status continuously.
COMP_BREW_CTRL.title: Brew Controller Module

COMP_GPIO_DRV.content:
Driver for general-purpose I/O pins. Manages:

- Output: Pump motor control (on/off)
- Output: Brew valve solenoid (open/close)
- Input: Button inputs (directly active-low with internal pull-ups)
- Output: LED status indicators
COMP_GPIO_DRV.title: GPIO Driver

COMP_PWM_DRV.content:
Driver for PWM output generation. Controls the heating element via
variable duty cycle (0–100%) at 1 kHz switching frequency. Supports
soft-start ramp to prevent inrush current.
COMP_PWM_DRV.title: PWM Driver

COMP_SAFETY_MON.content:
Module performing continuous safety checks on temperature and water
level. Implements fail-safe shutdown procedures.
COMP_SAFETY_MON.title: Safety Monitor Module

COMP_SPI_DRV.content:
Driver for the SPI bus peripheral. Provides communication with the
front-panel display controller (OLED) for status and menu rendering.
Operates at 4 MHz with DMA for frame-buffer transfers.
COMP_SPI_DRV.title: SPI Driver

COMP_TEMP_CTRL.content:
Module responsible for PID-based temperature control. Interfaces:

- Input: Temperature sensor (ADC)
- Output: Heating element PWM control
- Safety: Reports temperature status to Safety Monitor
- Safety: Responds to emergency shutdown commands
COMP_TEMP_CTRL.title: Temperature Controller Module

COMP_UI_MODULE.content:
Module handling all user interactions including button debouncing, LED
status indicators, and display updates. Interfaces with the Brew
Controller to send user commands (strength selection, start/stop).
COMP_UI_MODULE.title: User Interface Module

FSR_BRAKE_CTRL_01.content:
Control algorithm robust against uncertainties of the brake dynamics model
and disturbances. Performance maintained under friction coefficient variations
(µ=0.2 to µ=1.0).
FSR_BRAKE_CTRL_01.title: Brake Controller Robust Algorithm

FSR_BRAKE_CTRL_02.content:
Fail-operational design of brake controller. Independent brake circuits with
separate power supplies. Each circuit capable of achieving minimum 0.3g deceleration.
FSR_BRAKE_CTRL_02.title: Brake Controller Fail-Operational Design

FSR_BRAKE_CTRL_03.content:
Monitoring of operational state of brake controller and process and report
to superordinate controller. Status reported every 10ms with fault detection <100ms.
FSR_BRAKE_CTRL_03.title: Brake Controller Operational Monitoring

FSR_BRAKE_PROC_01.content:
Brake controller must recognize brakes operating beyond design limits and
react appropriately. Maximum pressure, temperature, duty cycle monitoring
with protective actions.
FSR_BRAKE_PROC_01.title: Brake System Design Limits

FSR_BRAKE_PROC_02.content:
Monitoring of electrical and mechanical brake components with reporting to
VDC. Pad wear, fluid level, actuator health, sensor status monitored continuously.
FSR_BRAKE_PROC_02.title: Brake Component Health Monitoring

FSR_DRIVE_CTRL_01.content:
Control algorithm robust against uncertainties of the drive dynamics model
and disturbances. Torque control accuracy ±5% under all conditions.
FSR_DRIVE_CTRL_01.title: Drive Controller Robust Algorithm

FSR_DRIVE_CTRL_02.content:
Sufficiently precise and validated drive dynamics model. Process variables
must comply with the physical process state. Model verified across full
speed and torque range.
FSR_DRIVE_CTRL_02.title: Drive Controller Validated Model

FSR_DRIVE_CTRL_03.content:
Fail-operational design of drive controller. Graceful degradation to limp-home
mode with minimum 20% torque capability maintained.
FSR_DRIVE_CTRL_03.title: Drive Controller Fail-Operational Design

FSR_DRIVE_PROC_01.content:
Monitoring of electrical/mechanical drive components and report to WRDC.
Motor temperature, inverter status, gear health monitored at 50Hz.
FSR_DRIVE_PROC_01.title: Drive Component Monitoring

FSR_DRIVE_PROC_02.content:
Drive controller must recognize drive operating beyond design limits and
react appropriately. Overspeed, overcurrent, overtemperature protection active.
FSR_DRIVE_PROC_02.title: Drive System Design Limits

FSR_POWER_01.content:
Continuous and sufficient power supply for all safety-critical actuators.
Redundant power sources with automatic failover. Minimum hold-up time: 500ms.
FSR_POWER_01.title: Actuator Power Supply Continuity

FSR_POWER_02.content:
Continuous and sufficient power supply for VDC and WRDC. Independent power
domains with galvanic isolation. Voltage monitoring and brown-out protection.
FSR_POWER_02.title: Controller Power Supply Continuity

FSR_PROC_CONFLICT_01.content:
Control actions of the vehicle dynamics controller must target the same
vehicle motion. Coordination logic prevents conflicting brake/drive commands.
Maximum conflict resolution time: 10ms.
FSR_PROC_CONFLICT_01.title: Vehicle Dynamics Control Action Consistency

FSR_PROC_CONFLICT_02.content:
Exclusion of drive and brake actuation with conflicting targets. Hardware
interlocks prevent simultaneous brake and drive application >10% torque.
FSR_PROC_CONFLICT_02.title: Wheel Dynamics Brake-Drive Conflict Prevention

FSR_STEER_CTRL_01.content:
Control algorithm must be robust against uncertainties of the steering
dynamics model and disturbances. Algorithm shall maintain stability and
performance under model parameter variations of ±20%.
FSR_STEER_CTRL_01.title: Steering Controller Robust Control Algorithm

FSR_STEER_CTRL_02.content:
Sufficiently precise and validated steering dynamics model. Model accuracy
shall be verified through physical testing with maximum error <5% across
the operational envelope.
FSR_STEER_CTRL_02.title: Steering Controller Validated Dynamics Model

FSR_STEER_CTRL_03.content:
Fail-operational design of steering controller. Single-point failures shall
not cause loss of steering control. Redundant execution paths required.
FSR_STEER_CTRL_03.title: Steering Controller Fail-Operational Design

FSR_STEER_CTRL_04.content:
Operation must be provided in required cycle time and jitter. Control loop
execution time: 10ms ± 1ms. Maximum jitter: 500µs.
FSR_STEER_CTRL_04.title: Steering Controller Timing Requirements

FSR_STEER_PROC_01.content:
Electrical and mechanical design according to state of the art. Components
shall meet automotive standards (ISO 26262, ISO 16750).
FSR_STEER_PROC_01.title: Steering Mechanical Design

FSR_STEER_PROC_02.content:
Monitoring of electrical and mechanical components and report to superordinate
controller. Motor current, temperature, position sensor health monitored at 100Hz.
FSR_STEER_PROC_02.title: Steering Component Monitoring

FSR_STEER_SENS_01.content:
Inadequate or missing feedback must be recognized and compensated for.
Sensor plausibility checks with redundant measurements. Timeout detection: 50ms.
FSR_STEER_SENS_01.title: Steering Sensor Feedback Compensation

FSR_STEER_SENS_02.content:
Continuous and sufficient power supply for steering-internal sensors.
Redundant power supply with automatic switchover <10ms.
FSR_STEER_SENS_02.title: Steering Sensor Power Supply

FSR_STEER_SENS_03.content:
Sufficient measurement accuracy for steering operation. Position accuracy:
±0.5°, velocity accuracy: ±1°/s.
FSR_STEER_SENS_03.title: Steering Sensor Measurement Accuracy

FSR_VDC_CTRL_01.content:
Control algorithm robust against uncertainties of the vehicle dynamics model
and disturbances. Trajectory tracking error <0.5m at speeds up to 130 km/h.
FSR_VDC_CTRL_01.title: VDC Robust Control Algorithm

FSR_VDC_CTRL_02.content:
Sufficiently precise and validated vehicle dynamics model. Process variables
must comply with the physical process state. Model validated through
hardware-in-the-loop testing.
FSR_VDC_CTRL_02.title: VDC Validated Dynamics Model

FSR_VDC_CTRL_03.content:
Fail-operational design of vehicle dynamics controller. Dual-redundant
processing with diverse algorithms. Cross-checking every cycle.
FSR_VDC_CTRL_03.title: VDC Fail-Operational Design

FSR_VDC_CTRL_04.content:
Fault-tolerant vehicle dynamics control algorithm capable of handling
degraded actuation (e.g., loss of one steering actuator or brake circuit).
FSR_VDC_CTRL_04.title: VDC Fault-Tolerant Algorithm

FSR_VEHICLE_SENS_01.content:
Inadequate or missing feedback must be recognized. Sensor fusion from multiple
sources (IMU, wheel speeds, GNSS). Fault detection within 100ms.
FSR_VEHICLE_SENS_01.title: Vehicle Motion Sensor Feedback

FSR_VEHICLE_SENS_02.content:
Sufficient measurement accuracy for vehicle dynamics control. Lateral
acceleration: ±0.1 m/s², yaw rate: ±0.5°/s, velocity: ±0.1 m/s.
FSR_VEHICLE_SENS_02.title: Vehicle Motion Sensor Accuracy

FSR_VEHICLE_SENS_03.content:
Updated feedback available in required cycle time and jitter. Sensor data
age <10ms, synchronized across all sensors with <1ms skew.
FSR_VEHICLE_SENS_03.title: Vehicle Motion Sensor Timing

FSR_WHEEL_SENS_01.content:
Inadequate or missing wheel speed feedback must be recognized and compensated.
Redundant sensing per wheel with plausibility checking against vehicle sensors.
FSR_WHEEL_SENS_01.title: Wheel Motion Sensor Compensation

FSR_WHEEL_SENS_02.content:
Continuous and sufficient power supply for wheel motion sensors. Battery-backed
power during transients. Voltage regulation ±5%.
FSR_WHEEL_SENS_02.title: Wheel Motion Sensor Power

FSR_WRDC_CTRL_01.content:
Fault-tolerant wheel rotational dynamics control algorithm. Algorithm shall
detect and compensate for single wheel actuator failures while maintaining
vehicle stability.
FSR_WRDC_CTRL_01.title: WRDC Fault-Tolerant Algorithm

FSR_WRDC_CTRL_02.content:
Fail-operational design of wheel rotational dynamics controller. Redundant
processing elements with cross-monitoring. Switchover time <20ms.
FSR_WRDC_CTRL_02.title: WRDC Fail-Operational Design

FSR_WRDC_CTRL_03.content:
Sufficiently precise and validated wheel rotational dynamics model. Tire
friction estimation accuracy ±10% across all surface conditions.
FSR_WRDC_CTRL_03.title: WRDC Precise Dynamics Model

FSR_WRDC_CTRL_04.content:
Operation must be provided in required cycle time and jitter. Control loop:
5ms ± 0.5ms. Anti-lock/anti-spin response time <20ms.
FSR_WRDC_CTRL_04.title: WRDC Timing Requirements

HAZ_TRAJ_DEV.content:
The vehicle deviates from its intended trajectory, potentially resulting in
collision with other traffic participants or stationary objects.

This is the fundamental hazard for vehicle actuation systems in automated
driving. When the actuation system fails to execute the trajectory commands
correctly, the vehicle may:

- Depart from the intended lane
- Collide with obstacles or other vehicles
- Fail to maintain safe following distance
- Execute unintended maneuvers

**ASIL Rationale:** This hazard is assigned **ASIL D** as the highest safety
integrity level because trajectory deviation during automated driving can lead
to severe accidents with life-threatening consequences. The assessment considers:

- **Severity (S3):** Life-threatening injuries or fatalities are likely outcomes
  of trajectory deviation, especially at highway speeds
- **Exposure (E4):** Trajectory control is continuously active during all automated
  driving operations
- **Controllability (C2-C3):** Limited ability for intervention in SAE Level 4/5
  automation where no human driver is monitoring or ready to take over

According to ISO 26262-3 Table 4, the combination of S3 + E4 + C2/C3 results
in ASIL D classification.
HAZ_TRAJ_DEV.scenario: Automated driving on public roads (all operational scenarios)
HAZ_TRAJ_DEV.title: Vehicle Not Following Intended Trajectory

INTF_BREW_CTRL_STATUS.content:
**Provider**: Brew Controller Module

**Consumer**: Safety Monitor Module

**Description**: Heartbeat and fault status reported by the Brew
Controller to the Safety Monitor for fault detection.

**Data Elements**:

- module_id: uint8
- heartbeat_counter: uint32 (incremented each cycle)
- fault_flags: uint16 (bitfield of detected faults)
- water_level: uint8 (0-100%)

**Protocol**: Polled by safety monitor at 10Hz
INTF_BREW_CTRL_STATUS.title: Brew Controller Safety Status Interface

INTF_GPIO.content:
**Provider**: GPIO Driver

**Consumers**: User Interface Module, Brew Controller Module

**Description**: Digital I/O abstraction for discrete signals — pump
motor, brew valve, buttons, and LED indicators.

**Operations**:

- set_pin(pin: GpioPin, state: bool)
- read_pin(pin: GpioPin) → bool
- register_interrupt(pin: GpioPin, edge: Edge, callback: fn())

**Protocol**: Direct register-mapped API with interrupt support
INTF_GPIO.title: GPIO Interface

INTF_PWM_CTRL.content:
**Provider**: PWM Driver

**Consumer**: Temperature Controller Module

**Description**: Controls PWM output channels for heating element
regulation.

**Operations**:

- set_duty_cycle(channel: uint8, duty: uint16) — 0–10000 (0.01%
  resolution)
- enable(channel: uint8)
- disable(channel: uint8)

**Protocol**: Direct register-mapped API, immediate effect
INTF_PWM_CTRL.title: PWM Control Interface

INTF_SAFETY_CMD.content:
**Provider**: Safety Monitor Module

**Consumers**: Temperature Controller, Brew Controller

**Description**: Emergency shutdown commands from safety monitor to
all controlled subsystems.

**Commands**:

- EMERGENCY_STOP: Immediate shutdown (<100ms response required)
- RESUME_NORMAL: Clear emergency state after fault resolved

**Protocol**: Interrupt-driven with hardware watchdog backup, highest
priority
INTF_SAFETY_CMD.title: Safety Command Interface

INTF_SENSOR_DATA.content:
**Provider**: Hardware sensors (temperature, water level)

**Consumers**: Temperature Controller, Safety Monitor

**Description**: Raw sensor readings from hardware via ADC.

**Data Elements**:

- temp_sensor_raw: uint16 (ADC value 0-4095)
- water_level_raw: uint16 (ADC value 0-4095)
- sensor_timestamp: uint32 (milliseconds)

**Protocol**: ADC DMA with double buffering, 100Hz sampling rate
INTF_SENSOR_DATA.title: Sensor Data Interface

INTF_SPI_BUS.content:
**Provider**: SPI Driver

**Consumer**: User Interface Module

**Description**: SPI bus access for communication with the front-panel
OLED display controller.

**Operations**:

- transfer(tx_buf: &[u8], rx_buf: &mut [u8])
- write_dma(buf: &[u8]) — non-blocking DMA transfer
- busy() → bool

**Protocol**: Full-duplex SPI Mode 0, 4 MHz clock, DMA-capable
INTF_SPI_BUS.title: SPI Bus Interface

INTF_TEMP_CTRL_STATUS.content:
**Provider**: Temperature Controller Module

**Consumer**: Safety Monitor Module

**Description**: Heartbeat and fault status reported by the
Temperature Controller to the Safety Monitor for fault detection.

**Data Elements**:

- module_id: uint8
- heartbeat_counter: uint32 (incremented each cycle)
- fault_flags: uint16 (bitfield of detected faults)
- temperature_value: int16 (current measured temperature)

**Protocol**: Polled by safety monitor at 10Hz
INTF_TEMP_CTRL_STATUS.title: Temperature Controller Safety Status Interface

INTF_TEMP_STATUS.content:
**Provider**: Temperature Controller Module

**Consumer**: Brew Controller Module

**Description**: Provides current temperature readings and heating
status to the brew controller.

**Data Elements**:

- current_temp: int16 (°C × 10 for 0.1°C resolution)
- target_temp: int16 (°C × 10)
- is_ready: bool (true when within target range)
- heating_active: bool

**Protocol**: Shared memory with atomic updates, 100ms refresh rate
INTF_TEMP_STATUS.title: Temperature Status Interface

INTF_USER_CMD.content:
**Provider**: User Interface Module

**Consumer**: Brew Controller Module

**Description**: User commands and settings passed from UI to the
brewing state machine.

**Commands**:

- START_BREW(strength: enum {WEAK, MEDIUM, STRONG})
- STOP_BREW
- SELECT_STRENGTH(strength: enum)

**Protocol**: Message queue with event-driven processing, debounced at
UI layer
INTF_USER_CMD.title: User Command Interface

shutdown procedures.

   :implements: SWREQ_WATER_LEVEL, SWREQ_OVERTEMP_SHUTDOWN
   :uses: INTF_TEMP_CTRL_STATUS, INTF_BREW_CTRL_STATUS, INTF_SENSOR_DATA
   :startup_calls: SEQSTART_04, SEQSTART_06, SEQSTART_08, SEQSTART_10
   :shutdown_calls: SEQSHTDWN_02, SEQSHTDWN_04, SEQSHTDWN_06
   :collapse: true
   :template: component_arch

   Module performing continuous safety checks on temperature and water
   level. Implements fail-safe shutdown procedures.

.. interface:: Safety Command Interface
   :id: INTF_SAFETY_CMD
   :status: open
   :tags: interface, safety
   :provided_by: COMP_SAFETY_MON
   :collapse: true

   **Provider**: Safety Monitor Module

   **Consumers**: Temperature Controller, Brew Controller

   **Description**: Emergency shutdown commands from safety monitor to
   all controlled subsystems.

   **Commands**:

   - EMERGENCY_STOP: Immediate shutdown (<100ms response required)
   - RESUME_NORMAL: Clear emergency state after fault resolved

   **Protocol**: Interrupt-driven with hardware watchdog backup, highest
   priority

SEQSHTDWN_01.content:
ADC Driver reports temperature exceeding 100 °C threshold to Safety
Monitor via ``INTF_SENSOR_DATA`` (polled every 100 ms).
SEQSHTDWN_01.title: temp=102°C (INTF_SENSOR_DATA — over-temp)

SEQSHTDWN_02.content:
Safety Monitor broadcasts ``EMERGENCY_STOP`` on ``INTF_SAFETY_CMD`` to
Temperature Controller; response required within 100 ms.
SEQSHTDWN_02.title: EMERGENCY_STOP → Temp Controller

SEQSHTDWN_03.content:
Temperature Controller confirms shutdown and reports ``FAULT_OVERTEMP``
flag via ``INTF_TEMP_CTRL_STATUS``.
SEQSHTDWN_03.title: fault_flags=OVERTEMP (INTF_TEMP_CTRL_STATUS)

SEQSHTDWN_04.content:
Safety Monitor broadcasts ``EMERGENCY_STOP`` on ``INTF_SAFETY_CMD`` to
Brew Controller; brew cycle aborted, pump stopped.
SEQSHTDWN_04.title: EMERGENCY_STOP → Brew Controller

SEQSHTDWN_05.content: Brew Controller confirms abort and reports ``FAULT_ABORT`` flag via ``INTF_BREW_CTRL_STATUS``.
SEQSHTDWN_05.title: fault_flags=ABORT (INTF_BREW_CTRL_STATUS)

SEQSHTDWN_06.content:
Safety Monitor notifies UI Module of over-temperature fault; UI
illuminates the Error LED and displays the fault message.
SEQSHTDWN_06.title: fault_event(OVERTEMP)

SEQSTART_01.content: ADC driver initialisation call from UI Module.
SEQSTART_01.title: init()

SEQSTART_02.content: ADC Driver confirms successful calibration to UI Module.
SEQSTART_02.title: init_ok

SEQSTART_03.content: UI Module requests Safety Monitor to start and run pre-checks.
SEQSTART_03.title: start() — Safety Monitor

SEQSTART_04.content: Safety Monitor polls ADC Driver for initial sensor readings.
SEQSTART_04.title: read_sensors()

SEQSTART_05.content:
ADC Driver returns ``INTF_SENSOR_DATA`` values; Safety Monitor asserts
pre-conditions (temp < 100 °C, water > threshold).
SEQSTART_05.title: temp=22°C, water_level=85%

SEQSTART_06.content: Safety Monitor starts Temperature Controller Module.
SEQSTART_06.title: start() — Temp Controller

SEQSTART_07.content: Temperature Controller confirms startup via heartbeat on ``INTF_TEMP_CTRL_STATUS``.
SEQSTART_07.title: started (INTF_TEMP_CTRL_STATUS heartbeat)

SEQSTART_08.content: Safety Monitor starts Brew Controller Module.
SEQSTART_08.title: start() — Brew Controller

SEQSTART_09.content: Brew Controller confirms startup via heartbeat on ``INTF_BREW_CTRL_STATUS``.
SEQSTART_09.title: started (INTF_BREW_CTRL_STATUS heartbeat)

SEQSTART_10.content:
Safety Monitor signals system readiness to UI Module; UI illuminates
the Ready LED.
SEQSTART_10.title: system_ready

SG_01.content:
The Vehicle Dynamics Controller must set a new target wheel torque when
required for safe trajectory following. Failure to provide necessary torque
commands can result in trajectory deviation.
SG_01.safe_state: Maintain current vehicle state with controlled deceleration
SG_01.title: VDC Must Set Target Wheel Torque When Required

SG_02.content:
The Vehicle Dynamics Controller must set a new target wheel torque only when
required. Unintended torque changes can cause unexpected vehicle behavior.
SG_02.title: VDC Must Set Target Wheel Torque Only When Required

SG_03.content:
The Vehicle Dynamics Controller must set a new target steering angle when
required for trajectory execution. Missing steering commands prevent proper
path following.
SG_03.safe_state: Maintain current steering angle with gradual return to center
SG_03.title: VDC Must Set Target Steering Angle When Required

SG_04.content:
The Vehicle Dynamics Controller must set a new target steering angle only when
required. Unintended steering changes are hazardous to vehicle control.
SG_04.safe_state: Maintain intended steering angle, reject spurious commands
SG_04.title: VDC Must Set Target Steering Angle Only When Required

SG_05.content:
The Wheel Rotational Dynamics Controller must change target brake torque when
required for proper vehicle speed control along the trajectory.
SG_05.title: WRDC Must Change Target Brake Torque When Required

SG_06.content:
The Wheel Rotational Dynamics Controller must change target brake torque only
when required. Unintended braking can cause trajectory deviation or collision.
SG_06.title: WRDC Must Change Target Brake Torque Only When Required

SG_07.content:
The Wheel Rotational Dynamics Controller must change target drive torque when
required for maintaining the planned velocity profile.
SG_07.safe_state: Maintain current speed with controlled adjustment
SG_07.title: WRDC Must Change Target Drive Torque When Required

SG_08.content:
The Wheel Rotational Dynamics Controller must change target drive torque only
when required to prevent unintended acceleration or deceleration.
SG_08.title: WRDC Must Change Target Drive Torque Only When Required

SG_09.content:
Anti-lock control must be performed only when wheel lock is imminent. Unnecessary
ABS activation can reduce braking efficiency and affect trajectory control.
SG_09.title: Anti-lock Control Must Be Performed Only When Required

SG_10.content:
Anti-lock control must be performed when required to prevent wheel lock during
braking, maintaining vehicle controllability.
SG_10.safe_state: Activate ABS to prevent wheel lock and maintain steerability
SG_10.title: Anti-lock Control Must Be Performed When Required

SG_11.content:
Anti-spin control must be performed only when wheel spin is detected. Unnecessary
intervention can affect acceleration performance and trajectory execution.
SG_11.title: Anti-spin Control Must Be Performed Only When Required

SG_12.content:
Anti-spin control must be performed when required to prevent excessive wheel spin
during acceleration, ensuring stable trajectory following.
SG_12.safe_state: Activate ASR to prevent wheel spin and maintain traction
SG_12.title: Anti-spin Control Must Be Performed When Required

SG_13.content:
The Drive Controller must apply drive torque when required to execute the
commanded velocity profile along the trajectory.
SG_13.safe_state: Maintain minimum safe speed or controlled stop
SG_13.title: Drive Controller Must Apply Drive Torque When Required

SG_14.content:
The Drive Controller must apply drive torque only when required. Unintended
drive torque can cause dangerous acceleration.
SG_14.safe_state: Zero torque or engine braking only
SG_14.title: Drive Controller Must Apply Drive Torque Only When Required

SG_15.content:
The Brake Controller must engage brake when required for deceleration or
emergency stopping to prevent collision.
SG_15.title: Brake Controller Must Engage Brake When Required

SG_16.content:
The Brake Controller must engage brake only when required. Unintended braking
can cause loss of vehicle control or rear-end collisions.
SG_16.title: Brake Controller Must Engage Brake Only When Required

SG_17.content:
The Steering Controller must change steering angle when required to follow
the commanded path. Failure prevents proper trajectory execution.
SG_17.safe_state: Gradual return to neutral steering position
SG_17.title: SC Must Change Steering Angle When Required

SG_18.content:
The Steering Controller must change steering angle only when required.
Unintended steering changes are extremely hazardous.
SG_18.title: SC Must Change Steering Angle Only When Required

SG_19.content:
The Steering Controller must hold steering angle when required to maintain
straight-line travel or constant-radius turns.
SG_19.title: SC Must Hold Steering Angle When Required

SG_20.content:
The Steering Controller must hold steering angle only when required. Locked
steering prevents necessary corrections and causes trajectory deviation.
SG_20.title: SC Must Hold Steering Angle Only When Required

SWREQ_TEMP_REGULATION.content:

SYSREQ_BRAKE_01.content:
The brake system shall implement X-split dual hydraulic circuits (FL-RR,
FR-RL) with independent pressure generation and control. Each circuit shall
be capable of achieving minimum 0.3g deceleration independently. Electronic
control units are dual-redundant with independent power supplies.
SYSREQ_BRAKE_01.title: Brake Dual-Circuit Hydraulic Architecture

SYSREQ_BRAKE_02.content:
The brake controller shall adapt pressure modulation strategy based on
estimated surface friction coefficient across full range µ=0.2 (ice) to
µ=1.0 (dry asphalt). Adaptation includes: brake force distribution, pressure
ramp rates, and ABS threshold tuning. Transition time between friction
regimes: <100ms.
SYSREQ_BRAKE_02.title: Brake Surface Friction Adaptation

SYSREQ_BRAKE_03.content:
The brake system shall continuously monitor: brake pad wear (thickness sensors),
hydraulic fluid level and pressure, brake disc temperature (IR sensors),
actuator health (current, position feedback, response time). Monitoring cycle:
100ms. Fault detection and reporting to VDC within 200ms.
SYSREQ_BRAKE_03.title: Brake Component Monitoring System

SYSREQ_DRIVE_01.content:
The drive controller shall maintain torque control accuracy ±5% of commanded
value across full speed-torque envelope: 0-200 km/h, -100% to +100% torque
(regen to full power). Control bandwidth: 20Hz. Response time from command
to 90% torque achievement: <150ms.
SYSREQ_DRIVE_01.title: Drive Torque Control System

SYSREQ_DRIVE_02.content:
The drive system shall implement fail-operational architecture with graceful
degradation to limp-home mode upon component failure. Limp-home mode capabilities:
minimum 20% of maximum torque, maximum speed 30 km/h, sufficient power to
reach safe stopping location. Mode transition time: <500ms.
SYSREQ_DRIVE_02.title: Drive Limp-Home Mode Architecture

SYSREQ_DRIVE_03.content:
The drive controller shall implement protection systems: (1) Overspeed: limit
at 210 km/h with soft cutoff; (2) Overcurrent: inverter current limit with
10µs response time; (3) Overtemperature: motor 180°C, inverter 125°C with
thermal derating starting at 80% limits. All limits shall trigger safe state
transition and fault reporting.
SYSREQ_DRIVE_03.title: Drive Electrical and Thermal Protection

SYSREQ_STEER_01.content:
The steering controller shall implement H-infinity robust control algorithm
with guaranteed stability and performance under parameter variations of ±20%
from nominal values. Parameters include: steering inertia, friction, assist
motor torque constant, and rack geometry. Control bandwidth: 10Hz minimum.
SYSREQ_STEER_01.title: Steering Robust Control Algorithm

SYSREQ_STEER_02.content:
The steering system shall use physics-based dynamics model validated through
physical testing with maximum modeling error <5% across operational envelope:
steering angle ±540°, steering rate ±200°/s, vehicle speed 0-130 km/h,
lateral acceleration ±8 m/s².
SYSREQ_STEER_02.title: Steering Validated Dynamics Model

SYSREQ_STEER_03.content:
The steering controller shall implement dual-channel architecture with
independent power supplies, processors, and motor windings. Each channel
capable of providing minimum 50% of maximum steering torque. Channels operate
in active-active mode with continuous cross-monitoring. Switchover time <10ms.
SYSREQ_STEER_03.title: Steering Redundant Execution Architecture

SYSREQ_STEER_04.content:
The steering system shall provide redundant position and velocity feedback
with specifications: position accuracy ±0.5° (absolute), velocity accuracy
±1°/s, update rate 1kHz, latency <1ms. Dual absolute encoders with diverse
sensing principles (magnetic + optical).
SYSREQ_STEER_04.title: Steering High-Resolution Feedback System

SYSREQ_VDC_01.content:
The VDC shall track the commanded trajectory with maximum lateral error ≤0.5m
and longitudinal error ≤0.3m at speeds up to 130 km/h under nominal conditions.
Performance degradation allowed under adverse conditions (reduced visibility,
low friction surfaces) with notification to supervision layer.
SYSREQ_VDC_01.title: VDC Trajectory Tracking Accuracy

SYSREQ_VDC_02.content:
The VDC shall implement dual-redundant processing with two independent processors
executing diverse control algorithms. Cross-checking shall occur every control
cycle (10ms) with automatic switchover to healthy processor within 20ms upon
detection of discrepancy >10%.
SYSREQ_VDC_02.title: VDC Dual-Redundant Processing Architecture

SYSREQ_VDC_03.content:
The VDC shall implement sensor fusion combining IMU (6-axis accelerometer/gyro),
individual wheel speed sensors, and GNSS/INS using Extended Kalman Filter.
System shall detect sensor failures within 100ms and maintain state estimation
with degraded accuracy using remaining sensors.
SYSREQ_VDC_03.title: VDC Multi-Sensor Fusion System

SYSREQ_VDC_04.content:
The VDC shall maintain trajectory control capability with single actuator or
sensor failure. Degraded modes: (1) Single wheel actuator failure: redistribute
torque to remaining wheels; (2) Steering actuator failure: trajectory control
via differential braking; (3) Single sensor failure: continue with reduced accuracy.
SYSREQ_VDC_04.title: VDC Graceful Degradation Controller

SYSREQ_WRDC_01.content:
The WRDC shall compensate for failed wheel actuator through coordinated control
of remaining three wheels. System shall detect actuator failure within 50ms
(via feedback comparison) and redistribute target torques to maintain yaw
stability within ±2° and lateral acceleration within ±0.5 m/s² of commanded values.
SYSREQ_WRDC_01.title: WRDC Single Wheel Fault Tolerance

SYSREQ_WRDC_02.content:
The WRDC shall implement real-time tire-road friction coefficient (µ) estimation
with ±10% accuracy across all surface conditions (dry asphalt µ=1.0 to ice µ=0.2).
Estimation algorithm shall use wheel slip ratio, longitudinal/lateral forces,
and vehicle dynamics model. Update rate: 100Hz.
SYSREQ_WRDC_02.title: WRDC Tire Friction Estimation System

SYSREQ_WRDC_03.content:
The WRDC shall implement integrated anti-lock braking (ABS) and anti-slip
regulation (ASR) with coordinated control logic. Wheel lock detection threshold:
slip ratio >0.15. Wheel spin detection threshold: slip ratio >0.10. Control
response time from detection to pressure modulation: <20ms.
SYSREQ_WRDC_03.title: WRDC ABS/ASR Coordination Logic

SYSREQ_WRDC_04.content:
The WRDC control loop shall execute with 5ms cycle time and maximum jitter
±0.5ms. Sensor data age shall not exceed 10ms. Anti-lock and anti-spin response
time from wheel slip detection to first pressure modulation: <20ms.
SYSREQ_WRDC_04.title: WRDC High-Frequency Control Loop

TEST_BREW_STRENGTH.content:
**Objective**: Verify all three strength settings produce correct
timing and water volume.

**Test Cases**:

- Weak: Assert 180ml water dispensed in 3 min ±5s
- Medium: Assert 180ml water dispensed in 4 min ±5s
- Strong: Assert 180ml water dispensed in 5 min ±5s
TEST_BREW_STRENGTH.title: Test Brew Strength Settings

TEST_BUTTON_DEBOUNCE.content:
**Objective**: Verify button handler correctly debounces rapid inputs.

**Steps**:

1. Simulate 10 button presses within 200ms
2. Count triggered events

**Expected**: Only 1-2 events triggered (first press + possible bounce
after 50ms timeout).
TEST_BUTTON_DEBOUNCE.title: Test Button Debouncing

TEST_E2E_BREWING.content:
**Objective**: Verify complete brewing cycle from user input to coffee
output.

**Steps**:

1. Select medium strength
2. Press start button
3. Monitor temperature, water flow, and timing

**Expected**: System heats to 85-95°C, dispenses 180ml over 4 minutes,
returns to idle state, no safety triggers.
TEST_E2E_BREWING.title: Test End-to-End Brewing
